boundaries: Source C is the authority: shared macros, includes, runtime capability changes and firmware restrictions remain explicit
Data carries per-model cells/references/default/domain evidence. Global type/unit/meaning authority belongs Architecture, not this JSON
Source includes virtual/proxy/simulator entries; do not label every row as physical hardware
All possible means finite pinned public radio surface plus scanned namespaced metadata declarations. Future/vendor raw commands and firmware behavior remain open-ended

semantics.declared-mask-member: Source mask after partial token macro expansion; not runtime support proof; unknown symbols retained.
semantics.declared-table-member: Source table membership after token filter where resolved; actual get/set and firmware restrictions remain handler-specific.
semantics.defaults: Metadata defaults are not actual hardware startup values. NULL/empty do not invent values.
common_unresolved: C conditional compilation and unresolved aliases/macros
Firmware, physical options and region-specific applicability
Dynamic capability probing or runtime model cloning
Actual observations, units and defaults absent source evidence
semantics.structured_values: Literal C initializer records/lists decoded as data; named symbols/macros stay unresolved. Sentinels retained explicitly; they are not available values. Positional shape follows the corresponding Architecture structured property record.
semantics.profile_ownership: Model selection data is not an added persisted profile field. Existing ProfileDocument owns configuration and endpoint intent; operating selections and actual observations remain separate.
semantics.port_vs_audio: CAT/PTT/DCD connection and radio audio/IQ streaming capabilities are distinct from PC capture/render device capabilities.
semantics.callback_bindings: Only actual rig_caps function-pointer declarations with nonzero source initializers appear in interactions. Data members and explicitly unbound initializers remain metadata.
semantics.unbound_callback_declarations: Explicit NULL/0/zero-mask initializer evidence is recorded separately, never counted as bound/callable nor inferred physical absence; frontend emulation remains separate.
semantics.table_resolution: Translation-unit-qualified table symbol first, shared backend family second, unique global third; cfgparams versus extparms roles come from actual model binding, not symbol spelling.
semantics.preprocessor_context: Source guards retained without evaluation; nonnull source initializer does not prove the declaration is active in a compiled build.

source_reference_format: file-id:line, resolved through source_files and provenance.baseline_commit

behavior.scope: Reference knowledge only; never C/JSON execution, runtime interpreter or replacement for project normative CAT authority/readback contracts.

method.binding_basis: Every nonnull interaction cell from corrected rig_caps actual-function-pointer whitelist catalogue; null/zero initializers are separate unbound provenance.
method.function_inventory: Lexical C/C++ function bodies under rigs/,src/,include/, including header definitions; conditional branches retained without preprocessing.
method.callgraph: Static lexical direct calls; same-file definitions, included headers, then same driver folder preferred before conservative global candidates. Pointer-field dispatch tracked separately. No compiler-proven reachability.
limitations: Macros, conditional compilation, alias expressions, dynamically assigned callbacks and transport handlers require contextual resolution.
All statically bound callbacks are indexed; all actually reachable runtime entrypoints are NOT claimed proven.
commented records identify extracted branch/error/state/dispatch evidence but are not complete behavioral formalizations.
Source body analysis does not verify physical radio behavior or firmware manuals.
Reference analysis does not establish compiled or physical behavior.

semantic_records.summary: Read addressed VFO receive/transmit frequency with targeted-command probing and fallback.
preconditions: Initialized Icom private state and valid output pointer.
Targetability, model topology, x25 probing state, memory mode and USB echo state affect path.

ordered_steps.semantics: Probe USB echo configuration if unknown; temporarily disable 731 four-byte mode for applicable memory reads.
TX alias first attempts direct TX-frequency query; fallback resolves TX/current VFO from routing snapshot.
When frequency is targetable and topology permits, query 0x25 with VFO number; record command availability.
If not targetable, forced swap, unavailable or first-probe rejection: save/select VFO, query 0x03 (loop limited to two attempts), restore saved VFO.
Interpret blank-memory 0xFF sentinel; remove command bytes and decode packed BCD frequency.
Accept 4,5,6-byte values; special three-byte ID-series values multiply by 10000 to obtain Hz; restore temporary 731 flag.

response_semantics: Returns decoded frequency or RIG_FREQ_NONE for recognized blank memory.
Targeted response has an extra VFO byte; offset differs from legacy read.
failure_semantics: Propagates transaction/selection/restoration errors.
Unexpected data length returns ENAVAIL or ETRUNC for empty-memory special case.
state_effects: May update echo/probe knowledge and temporarily select VFO.
Restoration is branch-specific; early exits do not establish universal restoration guarantee.
comments: The source tests freqbuf[4] in fallback retry although the transaction returns command/data layout; preserve as implementation evidence, not a protocol axiom.
semantic_records.ownership: physicalRadio interaction knowledge; backend owns execution

semantic_records.summary: Encode and set frequency with targeted/legacy fallback and model-specific recovery.

inputs.name: frequency
inputs.domain: Per-model range and mode tables; this handler is not a universal range validator.

preconditions: Initialized private state.

ordered_steps.semantics: Save current VFO; select requested VFO when required.
Read current frequency via rig_get_freq and abort on failure.
Encode frequency in little-endian packed BCD: four bytes in 731 mode, otherwise five; IC905 above 5.85 GHz uses six.
Try targeted 0x25 when permitted; unavailable target command falls back to 0x05 and restores saved VFO.
On failure during band change, if exchange operation exists, exchange VFOs and retry command; exchange back on retry failure.
Validate ACK when required; re-enable tone if backend tone_enable is set.

response_semantics: Required acknowledgement is one-byte ACK through icom_check_ack.
failure_semantics: Propagates read/transaction/exchange/restoration/ACK errors.
state_effects: Can affect current selection, probe state, frequency and tone.
Successful exchange recovery does not imply original VFO selection was restored.
comments: Current frequency is fetched but not used as a universal equality short-circuit.
No post-write frequency readback guarantee is provided by this handler.

When mode changes or width is not NOCHANGE, convert mode/filter; try 0x26 carrying base mode,data flag,filter. If failed, fallback 0x1A data-mode subcommand (IC7200 uses 0x04).
Width 1..3 explicitly selects filter. FM widths map through model fixed-filter thresholds.
Source returns OK early for width<=3; otherwise invoke DSP-filter helper if requested width differs or configured filter preference exists, then restore saved VFO.

response_semantics: Targeted helper performs ACK check; legacy-data fallback has distinct checks.
failure_semantics: Get-mode/conversion/selection errors propagate in specified branches.

semantic_records.summary: Classify Icom acknowledgement bytes.
preconditions: ackbuf has at least one readable byte even when ackLength=0, because failure logging reads ackbuf[0]; when ackLength>=2 the second byte must also be readable.
The declared length is nonnegative and does not exceed available readable storage.

ordered_steps.semantics: If length>=1 and first!=FB and length>=2 and second!=FA, return ETIMEOUT.
Otherwise if length!=1 or first!=FB return ERJCTED.
Otherwise return OK.

response_semantics: Success iff exactly one ACK byte FB.
failure_semantics: The compound timeout predicate is preserved exactly; one-byte NAK classifies ERJCTED.
state_effects: No state mutation.
comments: Classification only; no command state readback.
Zero declared length still accesses ackbuf[0] in debug logging at775; a length-sized zero-byte buffer is outside this scoped formalization.

semantic_records.summary: CI-V write, echo/collision handling, async demultiplexing and response extraction.
preconditions: Model private addressing and full-duplex/USB-echo state determine frame handling.
Null response-length means no answer expected.

ordered_steps.semantics: Mark transaction active; choose controller address E0 or80 by full-duplex capability; IC7100 flushes before writing.
Build/send CI-V envelope. If non-full-duplex and echo enabled, read echo, process async frames, ignore mismatched command/subcommand, compare echoed payload.
On collision retry up to20 times with500ms wait; missing echo yields BUSERROR; wrong echo length/content EPROTO.
If no answer expected clear active state and return OK.
Read answer while discarding matching echo and async frames; update detected USB echo state; skip AA-address frames.
Address mismatch can flush/retry; normalize single preamble; validate end marker, minimum frame length and NAK.
Extract response starting command byte at frame offset4, remove envelope and end byte; clear transaction-active flag.

response_semantics: Six-byte FE FE controller radio FA FD is command rejection.
Responses are command/data bytes without envelope.
failure_semantics: Transport failures propagate; collision BUSBUSY; missing echo BUSERROR; framing EPROTO; NAK ERJCTED; some async wait paths enforce configured timeout.
state_effects: Processes unsolicited radio status and updates echo knowledge.
Can retransmit physical writes during collision handling.
comments: Source contains TODO to check reply addresses; exact complete matching is not asserted.
Several goto/async paths and disabled preprocessor blocks remain partially modeled; retry write policy is reference only and must not override project no-write-replay rules.
semantic_records.ownership: RadioControlConnection/backend

semantic_records.summary: Read Icom base mode/filter and DSP width, distinguishing selected from other VFO.
preconditions: Targeted x26 allowed except IC7800 and forced topology swap.

ordered_steps.semantics: Query0x26 when targetable; response carries mode,data flag,filter; cache datamode/filter and adapt to legacy decode layout.
If x26 unavailable or first probing rejection query legacy0x04; validate resulting mode payload length1or2.
Use model i2r mapper or icom2rig_mode.
IC7300/MK2/9700/705 FM/PKTFM/WFM return mapped fixed width directly. Models without DSP-width querying return mapped preset.
For other modes selected VFO reads DSP width; nonselected VFO returns cached width.

response_semantics: IC7300 FM FIL1=15000Hz,FIL2=10000Hz,FIL3=7000Hz; DSP passbands may be cached for nonselected VFO.
failure_semantics: Transaction errors propagate; unexpected mode frame length ERJCTED.
state_effects: Updates backend filter/datamode; may query selected VFO DSP width.
comments: Cached nonselected passband is not independent physical readback.
The source rewrites mode_len and filter fields; preserve source algorithm rather than invent uniform response layout.

semantic_records.summary: Decode queried DSP passband index or return fallback/default marker.
preconditions: RTTY filter path depends on active RIG_FUNC_RF.
X108G/X5105/G90 force no1A03 support state.

ordered_steps.semantics: If RTTY filter active read enumerated extension; invalid/failing extension returns0 default.
If no1A03 support known return0. Query1A03 (IC7200 subcommand02).
On first rejection for nonIC7300/MK2 mark command unavailable and return0; later rejection may return error. Other transaction failure returns0 default.
Require3-byte response beginning1A; decode one-byte packed BCD index. AM rejects index>49 then width=(index+1)*200Hz.
SSB/CW/RTTY/packet-SSB return filtericom[index]; source boundary fallback sets index40 only for index greater than table element count.

response_semantics: Return0 is default/unknown, not zero-Hz physical passband.
failure_semantics: Some errors returned as negative width, most become0 default; AM bad index EPROTO.
state_effects: May mark1A03 unavailable.
comments: Potential equal-to-array-size boundary remains source evidence; no executable model or driver fix is proposed.

semantic_records.summary: ASCII terminated CAT transaction with verification command, IF cache and retry distinctions.
preconditions: Private command terminator,verify command,port retry and question-mark interpretation configured.

ordered_steps.semantics: Validate command/response arguments; mark active; emulation clears post-write delay.
IF query can return cached IF younger than500ms. Set-like command invalidates cache.
Allocate command buffer, append configured terminator unless already semicolon/CR, flush input then write.
RX,RU,RD,some KY,PS,K22 commands skip verification; most skip commands settle200ms. no_id allows no-reply return.
For ordinary no-response setters append verify_cmd to detect queued command errors.
Read terminated reply; on read failure or missing terminator retry write within port retry. Remove nonprintables when terminator printable.
N reply→ENAVAIL; O→retry then EPROTO; E→retry then EIO. Question mark may mean immediate ERJCTED or read-again with100ms wait then later rewrite after configured timeout.
Query reply must match first2command characters (single-char XG3 allowed; PS excepted); mismatched nonempty reply retries read while empty retries write.

response_semantics: Verification of separate command is not requested-setting readback.
failure_semantics: Memory allocation ENOMEM; argument EINVAL; protocol/error mapping above; remaining reply/copy/cache branches source-indexed.
state_effects: IF cache and transaction active state mutate; retries may replay writes.
comments: Partial: no universal exactly-once or complete active-state cleanup claim; some early returns bypass common cleanup.
This retry/replay behavior is reference knowledge only; station adapter normative no-replay/query policy remains authoritative.

semantic_records.summary: Generic getter may return cache, call targetable driver, or switch VFO around query.
preconditions: Valid rig/caps and non-null output.
Cache policy,morse busy,uplink,PTT,model,targetability and current VFO affect path.

ordered_steps.semantics: Resolve aliases; uplink-suppressed VFO,TX while not transmitting,or morse busy return cached frequency successfully.
For FTDX101D/IC910 A/Main in split, query PTT and return cache if transmitting.
Honor cache age/ALWAYS/use_cached_freq except IC9100 and WSJT-X precision-probe frequencies ending55or56Hz.
Require get_freq callback; invoke directly when targetable/current or special NETRIGCTL vfo_opt path.
For non-targeted read require set_vfo; unknown ID5100 current side gives ENTARGET; select target,read,attempt restore even on read failure.
Zero driver frequency may be replaced by cache; later compensation/LO/cache paths remain indexed in source.

response_semantics: Successful API getter alone does not prove fresh physical query.
failure_semantics: EINVAL arguments,ENAVAIL missing callback/selection capability,ENTARGET unsafe unknown restoration; driver errors propagate as source branches define.
state_effects: Can mutate cache/current VFO and consult PTT; query may temporarily change radio selection.
comments: Frontend cache shortcuts must not satisfy project-required physical CAT readback without freshness evidence.
semantic_records.ownership: RadioControlConnection/backend

semantic_records.summary: IC7300 receive frequency/base-data mode/filter/split specialization.
preconditions: Model identity RIG_MODEL_IC7300; capability defaults are source knowledge, firmware/settings may override context.

ordered_steps.semantics: Address94hex; five-byte little-endian BCD frequency under normal non731 mode. Targeted frequency/mode commands25hex/26hex always enabled in private capability.
Mode includes data flag; packet USB/LSB/FM/AM are base mode plus data flag; mode_with_filter supports filter byte.
Preserve selected filter around mode change because source documents default-FIL2 issue; width1..3 explicitly selects FIL1..3.
FM fixed FIL1/FIL2/FIL3 widths15k/10k/7kHz; other DSP passbands use1A03 quantized table.
Targeted split frequency avoids exchange; no_xchg=true suppresses regular exchange path. Split enable normally selects RX VFO and sends0F00/01.

response_semantics: Frequency/mode getter may inherit frontend/private cache shortcuts; selected/nonselected passband freshness differs.
failure_semantics: ACK/getter success from upstream is not project acceptance; required fresh query/readback and error authority remain normative.
state_effects: Frequency,mode,data flag,filter and split routing interact; these are reference state dimensions.
comments: This specialization does not assert firmware defect applicability was hardware verified.

semantic_records.summary: ADAT stages requested frequency in private state before command-list transaction.

inputs.name: vfo
inputs.use: Not consulted by this function body.

preconditions: For nonnull pRig, STATE(pRig)->priv must point to initialized ADAT private state.

ordered_steps.semantics: If pRig is NULL set return code to -RIG_EARG and skip state/transaction.
Otherwise obtain pPriv from STATE(pRig)->priv and assign pPriv->nFreq=freq BEFORE calling adat_transaction.
Invoke adat_transaction(pRig,&adat_cmd_list_set_freq). Descriptor sequence is display-off,set-frequency,get-frequency.
Return the transaction result; this wrapper does not roll back nFreq on failure.

response_semantics: Set command formatter uses private nFreq converted to int with $FR1: prefix and ADAT_EOM; transaction dispatches descriptor callbacks and stops on error.
The later get-frequency command can refresh private state if reached and successful; it is not guaranteed after an earlier failure.
failure_semantics: Null pRig gives EARG; transaction error is returned.
No range validation or VFO selection appears in this wrapper.
state_effects: Private requested frequency changes before device transaction; a failed transaction can leave staged requested value.
comments: Source-specific reviewed partial commentary. Full ADAT framing,response parsing,error recovery and delay semantics remain source-observed, not formalized here.

DATA A mode - DATA (REV) on LSB optimized for HF Packet, VFO dial is suppressed carrier QRG
DATA A mode - DATA on USB general, VFO dial is suppressed carrier QRG
FSK D mode - direct FSK on LSB optimized for RTTY, VFO dial is MARK

source_comment_evidence: if FB command than we change to FB and back again to avoid VFO blinking

TS590s f/w rev 1.07 or earlier has a defect that means frequency set on TX VFO in split mode may not be set correctly. The symptom of the defect is either TX on the wrong frequency (i.e. TX on a frequency different from that showing on the TX VFO) or no output. We use an IF command to find out if we have just set the "back" VFO when the rig is in split mode. If we have; we then read the other VFO and set it to what we read - a null transaction that fixes the defect.
split mode and setting "back" VFO
set other VFO to whatever it is at currently

source_comment_evidence: if this is an IF cmdstr and not the first time through check cache
500ms cache time
then we must be setting something so we'll invalidate the cache
only retry if we expect a response from the command
so in order to retry commands need to re-write them

The ? response is an ambiguous response, but for get commands it seems to indicate that the rig rejected the command because the state of the rig is not valid for the command or that the command parameter is invalid. Retrying the command does not fix the issue, as the error is caused by the invalid combination of command and rig state. For example, the following cases have been observed: - NL(NB level) and RL(NR level) commands fail if NB/NR are not enabled on TS-590SG - SH and SL (filter width) fail in CW mode on TS-590SG - GT (AGC) fails in FM mode on TS-590SG There are more cases like these and they vary by rig model.

source_comment_evidence: Based on AA6E research (no thanks to errors in TT Prog Ref Manual!) The "set" function ( K command) uses a different data format from the ?K get function. Data transferred to rig: +--+--+----------NB value (0-7) v v v +-------NB "on/off" bit |__|__|__|__| 8 4 2 1 The NB on/off bit corresponds to the "Noise Blanker" item in the Jupiter menu. The value is show in the "NB selection" item in the Jupiter menu. Note that if all zeroes are sent, the NB does shut off, but the NB value is unchanged. If you want to change the NB value, the on/off bit must be set. Because the on/off status cannot (apparently) be read back by software, we will leave NB always on, but set to zero value when NB "off" is desired. It is not clear if NB on/off makes a difference if the value is zero. (ver 1330-538 firmware)

source_comment_evidence: Snapshot VFO-B state for best-effort restore on exit. Responses (FB%09d; and MD1%c;) are already valid set commands and can be replayed verbatim. If the query fails, the saved_ buffer stays empty and restore is skipped.

1. Point the Sub-side MC cursor at the target slot. The MC SET form takes a VFO digit followed by a 5-digit channel (MC0NNNNN = Main, MC1NNNNN = Sub); BM commits VFO-B to the last-selected memory on the Sub side, so targeting Sub here keeps Main's front-panel channel from silently flipping. Returns '?;' when the slot is unprogrammed, but the cursor still updates for the subsequent BM.
2. Force VFO mode. Must be the 6-char form — extra digits are rejected by firmware.
3a. Program VFO-B frequency.
3b. Program VFO-B mode.
DCS: select CT mode 3, then program code via CN P2=1. (The DC command is firmware-broken — use CN instead.)
Explicit CT OFF in case VFO-B was previously configured with a tone.

3d. Clarifier (RIT/XIT). The FTX-1 uses one shared offset with independent RX/TX on-off toggles via the 11-char CF command: CF P1 P2 P3 P4 P5P5P5P5 ; where P3=0 sets RX/TX on/off (P4: 0=RX OFF, 1=RX ON, 2=TX OFF, 3=TX ON) and P3=1 sets the offset frequency (P4=+/-, P5P5P5P5 = offset Hz). If both rit and xit are set, rit's offset wins (matches the pre-#2034 behavior of the broken MW path). Note that the TX CLAR flag is silently dropped by BM (firmware limitation); we still emit it for forward compatibility.

source_comment_evidence: FTX1 split configuration: - Split ON: RX on MAIN, TX on SUB (the only supported config) - Split OFF: TX on MAIN (same as RX) CRITICAL: The Hamlib core's vfo_fixup() converts "Main" to "VFOA". Since VFOA and MAIN share the same cache slot (freqMainA), we MUST force tx_vfo to SUB when split is ON. Otherwise: 1. rig_set_split_freq caches TX freq for VFOA 2. This overwrites the MAIN cache with the TX frequency 3. rig_get_freq returns TX freq instead of RX freq By forcing tx_vfo=SUB here, and publishing the TX VFO, we ensure that subsequent rig_set_split_freq calls cache for SUB (not VFOA/MAIN). Note: The core may overwrite the TX routing state after this returns, but we also fix it in ftx1_set_split_freq as a backup.
